title: Company Secretary (CS)
description:
**About Quattro Group**

Quattro Group of Companies is a diversified business group with interests in commercial real estate, office leasing, managed workspaces, turnkey fit-outs, facility management, information technology and retail.

With multiple business entities and an expanding portfolio, the Group is looking for a competent and experienced Company Secretary to strengthen corporate governance, ensure regulatory compliance and support management in corporate and legal matters.

Key Responsibilities

**1. Corporate Secretarial & Statutory Compliance**

* Ensure compliance with the Companies Act, 2013 and applicable rules and regulations.
* Manage statutory filings, annual returns, financial statement filings and event-based compliances with the Registrar of Companies (ROC).
* Maintain statutory registers, records, minutes books and corporate documentation.
* Monitor compliance requirements across all Group companies, subsidiaries and associated entities.
* Coordinate with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA), ROC and other statutory authorities.

**2. Board Meetings & Corporate Governance**

* Organize Board Meetings, Annual General Meetings (AGMs) and Extraordinary General Meetings (EGMs).
* Prepare notices, agendas, resolutions, minutes and related documentation.
* Advise Directors and management on corporate governance requirements and statutory responsibilities.
* Maintain records of Board approvals, shareholder resolutions and delegated authorities.

**3. Legal & Commercial Documentation**

* Coordinate with internal and external legal counsel on corporate and commercial matters.
* Review and assist in preparing agreements, contracts, MOUs, NDAs, shareholder agreements and other legal documentation.
* Support documentation for real estate transactions, leasing arrangements, business partnerships and commercial contracts.
* Assist management in identifying contractual and regulatory risks.

**4. Group Structure & Corporate Transactions**

* Manage documentation relating to incorporation of new companies, changes in shareholding, appointment or resignation of Directors and capital restructuring.
* Support corporate restructuring, mergers, acquisitions and joint ventures, wherever applicable.
* Coordinate with auditors, bankers, consultants and regulatory authorities for corporate transactions.
* Maintain updated records of Group entities, ownership structures and authorized signatories.

**5. Compliance Monitoring & Risk Management**

* Develop and maintain a centralized compliance calendar for all Group entities.
* Track statutory deadlines, renewals, filings and approvals.
* Coordinate with Finance, HR, Legal and Operations teams to ensure timely compliance.
* Identify compliance gaps and recommend corrective actions.
* Provide periodic compliance status reports to Group management.

**6. Regulatory & Stakeholder Coordination**

* Liaise with statutory auditors, secretarial auditors, tax consultants, legal advisors and government authorities.
* Assist with due diligence exercises, corporate records and regulatory submissions.
* Support management on FEMA, RBI and other regulatory matters wherever applicable, in coordination with specialist advisors.

Required Qualifications & Experience

* Qualified Company Secretary and member of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI).
* 5–10 years of relevant post-qualification experience preferred.
* Strong knowledge of the Companies Act, 2013, MCA/ROC procedures and corporate governance.
* Experience managing statutory compliances for multiple companies.
* Working knowledge of corporate contracts, commercial documentation and regulatory requirements.
* Proficiency in MCA V3 portal, MS Office and compliance management systems.
* Experience in real estate, infrastructure, diversified business groups or multi-entity corporate structures will be an advantage.

Key Competencies

* Strong attention to detail and regulatory discipline.
* Excellent drafting, documentation and communication skills.
* Ability to independently manage multiple Group entities.
* High standards of confidentiality, integrity and professional ethics.
* Strong coordination skills with senior management, auditors, consultants and legal advisors.
* Proactive approach to identifying compliance risks and meeting statutory deadlines.

What We Offer

* Opportunity to work directly with Group leadership.
* Exposure to multiple businesses and corporate structures.
* A responsible role combining governance, legal coordination and strategic corporate support.
* Competitive compensation commensurate with qualifications and experience.

**Compensation:** As per industry standards and candidate experience

**Application:** Share your updated CV at hr@quattrospaces.com, mentioning "Application – Company Secretary" in the subject line.

Benefits:

* Paid sick time
* Provident Fund

Work Location: In person

title: Analyst II, Compliance
description:
**Position Type :**

Full time

**Type Of Hire :**

Experienced (relevant combo of work and education)

Are you curious, motivated, and thinking? At FIS, you’ll have the opportunity to work on some of the most challenging and relevant issues in financial services and technology. Our talented people empower us, and we believe in being part of a team that is open, collaborative, entrepreneurial, passionate and above all fun.

**About the team**

The Credentialing Team plays a vital role in protecting the organization by conducting client due diligence, credentialing reviews, and verification activities for new and existing customers. We partner with stakeholders across the business to ensure compliance with regulatory and contractual requirements while supporting safe, efficient, and compliant client onboarding and ongoing relationship management.

**What You Will Be Doing**

* Conduct credentialing reviews for Financial Institution (FI) and Non-Financial Institution (Non-FI) clients to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, internal policies, and contractual obligations.
* Evaluate client documentation, perform due diligence reviews, and validate business legitimacy using internal systems, public records, and approved verification sources.
* Manage implementation, risk-based, and branch verification credentialing activities for new contracts, contract amendments, renewals, and new branch locations.
* Perform background checks and cross-reference information against various databases and official sources to identify potential compliance risks and ensure data integrity.
* Analyze credentialing requests, identify exceptions or risk indicators, and escalate complex cases to leadership when necessary.
* Maintain accurate case records, trackers, and supporting documentation while ensuring compliance with established service level agreements (SLAs) and quality standards.
* Partner with internal stakeholders including Contract Administration, Finance, Documentation Management, and Compliance teams to facilitate timely onboarding and re-credentialing activities.
* Monitor recurring credentialing requirements and support annual or periodic re-credentialing efforts to ensure client records remain current and compliant.
* Respond to credentialing-related inquiries through shared team mailboxes and provide professional support to internal and external customers.
* Contribute to process improvements, operational excellence initiatives, reporting activities, and audit readiness efforts that enhance the effectiveness of the compliance program.
* Assist in training and mentoring junior analysts by sharing subject matter expertise and promoting consistent execution of credentialing procedures.

**What You Bring**

* Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Compliance, Risk Management, or a related field.
* 2-5 years of experience in Compliance, Credentialing, KYC, Client Onboarding, Risk Management, Audit, Financial Services, or a related operational function.
* Working knowledge of client due diligence, credentialing, customer onboarding, and compliance risk assessment principles.
* Experience reviewing and validating business documentation, legal agreements, licensing information, and organizational records.
* Strong analytical and investigative skills with the ability to identify inconsistencies, assess risk indicators, and make sound recommendations.
* Experience conducting research and verification activities using public records, official websites, databases, and internal systems.
* Excellent attention to detail with the ability to manage multiple cases simultaneously while maintaining high levels of accuracy and quality.
* Demonstrated ability to interpret policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements and apply them consistently to business scenarios.
* Strong organizational and time management skills with the ability to meet service level agreements (SLAs) and competing deadlines.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to interact professionally with internal stakeholders and external clients.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Outlook, Word, and reporting tools.
* Ability to work independently, exercise professional judgment, and escalate complex or high-risk situations appropriately.
* Experience participating in process improvement initiatives, quality reviews, audits, or compliance monitoring activities.
* Strong collaboration skills with a proven ability to work effectively across cross-functional teams.

**What we offer you:**

  

* Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package.
* Professional growth and advancement opportunities.
* Exposure to global compliance, risk, and credentialing operations.
* Continuous learning, certification, and development programs.
* Collaborative and inclusive team environment.
* Flexible work arrangements and wellbeing initiatives.
* Recognition programs that celebrate performance and contributions.
* Opportunity to make a meaningful impact in protecting the integrity of client onboarding and compliance processes.

**Privacy Statement**

FIS is committed to protecting the privacy and security of all personal information that we process in order to provide services to our clients. For specific information on how FIS protects personal information online, please see the Online Privacy Notice.

**Sourcing Model**

Recruitment at FIS works primarily on a direct sourcing model; a relatively small portion of our hiring is through recruitment agencies. FIS does not accept resumes from recruitment agencies which are not on the preferred supplier list and is not responsible for any related fees for resumes submitted to job postings, our employees, or any other part of our company.

description:

The role will be responsible for handling a variety of work involving legal and regulatory aspects of non-banking financial business, insurance, treasury, new fintech products, drafting and streamlining of documentation and negotiations with regard to different types of agreements related to the credit and insurance business.
  
  
**Responsibilities:**  
Ability to work in a highly dynamic environment and collaboration with various internal and external stakeholders.
  
Ability to think through original new products, expansion into new market verticals and areas relating to innovative fintech and financial solutions.
  
The ability to provide time-sensitive support on a wide array of legal and regulatory issues in connection with all aspects of PayU's operations in India, along with the ability to conduct research and form views across different legislations and regulations governing various sectors in India.
  
Draft, review, and negotiate a wide range of commercial contracts, including non-disclosure agreements, service agreements, service level agreement, amendment agreements, memorandum of understanding, letter of intent etc.
  
Own the full contract lifecycle including drafting, redlining, negotiation, finalization, execution, and post-signing compliance.
  
Ensure contracts align with legal and regulatory requirements, corporate policies, and industry best practices.
  
Participate in contract negotiations with external parties including lending service providers, merchants, banks and financial institutions, vendors, demonstrating strong negotiation skills to achieve favorable terms and outcomes.
  
Develop and maintain contract templates and standard clauses to streamline the contract drafting process and contribute to playbooks, negotiation strategies, and process improvements to reduce contract closure timelines.
  
Assist the organization by keeping abreast of new legislation and regulatory developments that may impact the business.
  
Strong drafting and communication (both written and oral) skills in English.
  
**Key personalities:** Efficient, punctual, responsible, transparent, reliable and accountable.
  
  
**Requirements:**  
The ideal candidate will be an independent, result-oriented, self-motivated individual who enjoys working in a fast paced, international, dynamic, and diverse environment.
  
Bachelor’s degree in law from a recognized Indian institute.
  
5 to 7 years’ professional experience with a reputed law firm and/or reputable corporate entity or financial institution. Initial background of working with a law firm on M&A, general corporate, banking, capital markets, technology, intellectual property, privacy or financing legal work will be a definite plus.

Experience in Indian laws and regulations concerning one or more of payment aggregation, banking, NBFCs, digital payments, digital lending, insurance and financial services, fintech businesses, prepaid payment instruments, bill payments, and technology.
  
Experience in developing and implementing processes for efficient and streamlined operations surrounding contract negotiations and processes.

A positive, get-things-done workplace.
  
A dynamic, constantly evolving space (change is par for the course – important you are comfortable with this).

PayU, one of India's leading digital financial services providers with Prosus as an investor, operates businesses that are regulated by the Reserve Bank of India and offers advanced solutions to meet the digital payment and digital lending requirements of the Indian market. PayU India companies aim to create a full-stack digital financial services platform to serve all (tapped and untapped) financial needs of customers through technology solutions.
  
  
PayU Finance India Private Limited, is a non-deposit taking systemically important non-banking financial company registered with the Reserve Bank of India(“RBI”) vide certificate of registration (CoR) number 13.00127 dated 21 February 2019.
  
  
PayU Finance is engaged inter alia in the business of providing products, enterprise lending and specific lending, apart from providing certain technology related services, financial services, or a combination of both.

title: Analyst, Compliance & Risk Management
description:
JLL supports the Whole You, personally and professionally.
  
  
Our people at JLL are shaping the future of real estate for a better world by combining world class services, advisory and technology to our clients. We are committed to hiring the best, most talented people in our industry; and we support them through professional growth, flexibility, and personalized benefits to manage life in and outside of work. Whether you’ve got deep experience in commercial real estate, skilled trades, and technology, or you’re looking to apply your relevant experience to a new industry, we empower you to shape a brighter way forward so you can thrive professionally and personally.
  
  
What this job involves
  
  
The KYC / Sanctions Screening Analyst is a role under JLL’s Global Legal Compliance (GLC) team. The KYC / Sanctions Screening Analyst will be located in a JLL Business Services (JBS) shared service centre, and will report to the Compliance / Sanctions Screening Manager within JBS.
  
  
**The KYC / Sanctions Screening Analyst will be responsible for:**
  
Offering compliant workarounds / alternatives where confronted by obstacles to complete AML KYC;
  
Reviewing and resolving false positives from automated daily ongoing screening;
  
Manual uploads of names for initial screening in JLL’s global sanctions screening system;
  
Extracting data from screening system and forwarding screening results to relevant parties within JLL;
  
Escalating potential true matches to appropriate parties within JLL, according to sanctions screening escalation procedures, for further investigation and resolution;
  
Ensuring screening procedures are followed consistently with a documented audit trail for all KYC / sanction match resolution actions taken;
  
Reviewing preliminary KYC / AML materials liaising with relevant business and local legal & compliance counterparties in line with JLL’s minimum global standards
  
  
**Sound like you? To apply you need to be:** –
  
  
The KYC / Sanctions Screening Analyst must have a good knowledge and understanding of sanction law requirements, AML Regulations and KYC best practices, in addition to good technical skills to be able to navigate JLL’s sanctions screening system, extract data from the system and forward to others for escalation and resolution procedures. This includes proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, and Adobe PDF. The Analyst must also be able to efficiently identify false matches and conduct initial investigation into potential true matches, and must have good communication and organizational skills to work with local Legal & Compliance teams and continuously follow up on open cases through proper resolution of potential matches identified in the system.
  
  
The AML checks to be conducted on Clients and counterparties which will include: (i) listed companies (and their subsidiaries), (ii) regulated companies (and their subsidiaries), (iii) private individuals and families, (iv) trusts, foundations and unincorporated associated, (v) governments and public authorities, (vi) private and unlisted companies (including special purpose vehicles).
  
An ability to navigate JLL’s Customer Relationship Management (e.g. Salesforce, MS Dynamics) and AML KYC systems (e.g. World Check, Bureau Van Dyke), extract data from the system and forward to others for escalation and resolution procedures is important. This includes proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, and Adobe PDF.
  
The Analyst must also be able to identify false matches efficiently and conduct initial investigation into potential true matches of PEPs / Sanctions / Negative, and must have good communication and organisational skills to work with the EMEA AML Team and continuously follow up through to conclusion any open AML KYC checks
  
  
Key skills
  
  

* Prior experience with a large multinational financial institution in respect of sanctions screening and AML/KYC Checks, as well as familiarity with the US OFAC and other international sanctions laws is essential.
* Candidate needs to have some India specific AML experience, as well as familiarity with the other international sanctions laws is essential.
* Minimum 1 years’ experience with Global sanctions screening, Anti-Money Laundering, Know Your Client checks or compliance related field, and with a large multinational financial institution or similar.

Employee specification
  
  

* 2-year Associate’s Degree or equivalent.
* Strong understanding of OFAC and other international sanctions laws and Money Laundering Regulations.
* Good technical skills – proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook, and Adobe PDF and online research tools.
* Team player and self-starter with ability to work proactively and co-operatively with others.
* Excellent communications and problem-solving skills.
* Fluent English language skills essential – further language(s) beneficial
* Strong organisation and prioritization skills, to handle and keep track of high volume of records and cases.

**What we can do for you:**  
At JLL, we make sure that you become the best version of yourself by helping you realize your full potential in an entrepreneurial and inclusive work environment. We will empower your ambitions through our dedicated Total Rewards Program, competitive pay and benefits package.
  
  
Apply today!
  
If this job description resonates with you, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet all of the requirements below. We’re interested in getting to know you and what you bring to the table!
  
  
Personalized benefits that support personal well-being and growth:
  
  
JLL recognizes the impact that the workplace can have on your wellness, so we offer a supportive culture and comprehensive benefits package that prioritizes mental, physical and emotional health.
  
  
About JLL –
  
  
We’re JLL—a leading professional services and investment management firm specializing in real estate. We have operations in over 80 countries and a workforce of over 102,000 individuals around the world who help real estate owners, occupiers and investors achieve their business ambitions. As a global Fortune 500 company, we also have an inherent responsibility to drive sustainability and corporate social responsibility. That’s why we’re committed to our purpose to shape the future of real estate for a better world. We’re using the most advanced technology to create rewarding opportunities, amazing spaces and sustainable real estate solutions for our clients, our people, and our communities.
  
  
Our core values of teamwork, ethics and excellence are also fundamental to everything we do and we’re honored to be recognized with awards for our success by organizations both globally and locally.
  
  
Creating a diverse and inclusive culture where we all feel welcomed, valued and empowered to achieve our full potential is important to who we are today and where we’re headed in the future. And we know that unique backgrounds, experiences and perspectives help us think bigger, spark innovation and succeed together.

title: Company Secretary
description:
We are seeking a qualified Company Secretary to manage corporate compliance, secretarial functions, corporate governance, statutory filings, Board and shareholder matters, and coordination with legal advisors, auditors, regulators, and senior management.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Ensure compliance with the Companies Act, 2013, Rules, and applicable corporate laws.
* Monitor statutory changes and assess their impact on the Company.
* Prepare and file ROC, MCA, and other statutory forms, returns, and disclosures.
* Maintain statutory registers, secretarial records, and documentation.
* Ensure timely annual and event\-based filings.
* Coordinate with statutory authorities and regulators.
* Maintain the compliance calendar.

2\. Board \& Shareholder Management

* Organize Board Meetings, Committee Meetings, and General Meetings.
* Prepare agendas, notices, explanatory statements, and supporting documents.
* Draft and finalize Board and shareholder resolutions.
* Prepare and maintain meeting minutes.
* Ensure compliance with meeting timelines, quorum, and voting requirements.
* Maintain records of directors, Board composition, and committees.

3\. Corporate Governance

* Support sound corporate governance practices.
* Ensure compliance with related\-party transaction requirements.
* Maintain director and Key Managerial Personnel disclosures.
* Monitor conflicts of interest and governance matters.

4\. Fundraising \& Corporate Transactions

* Support equity and debt fundraising transactions.
* Handle secretarial documentation for private placements, rights issues, preferential allotments, share transfers, securities issuance, and ESOPs.
* Support investments, acquisitions, due diligence, and corporate restructuring.
* Maintain capitalization tables and shareholding records.

5\. Legal Documentation \& RBI Compliance

* Coordinate implementation of Shareholders' Agreements, Share Subscription Agreements, Investment Agreements, ESOP documentation, and other corporate agreements.
* Track contractual obligations and compliance requirements.
* Coordinate with external legal counsel.
* Support RBI/FEMA\-related compliances, foreign investment filings, and coordination with Authorized Dealer Banks, wherever applicable.

6\. Audit \& Compliance Monitoring

* Coordinate with Secretarial Auditors, Statutory Auditors, Internal Auditors, and legal advisors.
* Support due diligence and audit documentation.
* Track and close audit observations.
* Maintain compliance trackers and escalate potential compliance gaps.

**Qualifications \& Experience**

* Qualified Company Secretary (Member of ICSI).
* 1\-2 years of relevant post\-qualification experience.
* Experience in a CS Firm, startup, private equity/venture capital\-backed company, or high\-growth organization is preferred.
* Additional qualification in Law/LLB is an advantage.
* Exposure to fundraising, investor documentation, SHA/SSA, ESOP, and RBI compliance is an advantage.

**Required Skills**

* Strong knowledge of the Companies Act, 2013\.
* Understanding of corporate governance and Board processes.
* Strong drafting and documentation skills.
* Ability to interpret legal and commercial agreements.
* Good stakeholder management and communication skills.
* High attention to detail and ability to manage multiple deadlines.

**Key Performance Indicators**

* Timely statutory and secretarial filings.
* Timely conduct of Board, Committee, and Shareholder Meetings.
* Accuracy of Board minutes and resolutions.
* Effective compliance calendar management.
* Timely closure of audit and compliance observations.

**How to Apply:** Interested candidates may share their updated CV with **jobs@souave.com**.

Work Location: In person
